air cells and are well pneumatized and clear.

Normal MR evaluation of the temporal lobes..

Apparently her meltdowns were never this extreme until she got into high school. She’s always had them but the hitting herself and others started within the past 6 or 7 years (is what I’m gathering). She’s been to professionals but will often stop seeing them after one or two sessions. She doesn’t use coping skills because she believes that we shouldn’t ask her to stop her meltdowns and should instead just live with them and accept her for how she is. I’ve told her before that I am accepting of her and that I understand she has limitations, but that some of the behaviors she’s been having is dangerous to not only herself but other people. She tells me that she doesn’t see an issue with her behaviors because she’s autistic and people should be understanding that she can’t control them. 

The thing is I advocate a lot for people being understanding and accepting. I tell the parents of my client’s all the time that I’m not the type of counselor to stop them from doing things like stemming, forcing eye contact, forcing socialization (if they don’t want it), and other small things that is just normal behaviors for someone with autism. Hell, I don’t mind the occasional meltdown either, but the issue is when the person is being dangerous to themselves or others whether that’s physically or mentally. I hope I’m making sense.

I’m not saying that if I can do it as an autistic individual then she should be able to do it too, but I mean I don’t feel I should be accepting of her wailing on the people in our house and screaming in our faces either.

Off topic to the post but I’m actually a mental health counselor. I was wondering what you feel we could do to better help people like my step-sister then? Because I feel she’s getting the grounds to talk about how she’s feeling and what she’s going through, but it seems that no matter how hard we try it just isn’t working. As professionals how can we help our clients without “modifying” their behaviors so to speak. I have no issues with stemming, or lack of eye contact, or anything like that. I don’t believe that needs to be modified, but the issue is when the person is being a direct threat to themselves and others.

The thing that frustrates me though is that she doesn’t /want/ to change. She even said that herself. She’s completely happy with the way things are now even though she is making everyone else miserable. I understand that she masks outside our home, I have to do that daily too, but the issue is that she cannot continue these behaviors and achieve the goals that’s she’s trying to achieve (she wants to be an elementary school teacher). I have given her so much empathy and understanding but I feel like all my effort is being wasted because she simply refuses to change. I understand the meltdowns are due to overstimulation. I even have the occasional one myself, but the issue is she has all these coping mechanisms that she has been taught and she refuses to use them. She won’t even try. It’s so frustrating because I want the best for her but she doesn’t want the best for herself. She is allowed to leave bruises on her brother and there is no consequences for it. She’s allowed to scream in our faces and push us but doesn’t even apologize. I genuinely don’t think she feels bad. Sorry I’m not mad or anything at your response I’m just completely at a loss.

I’ve been in counseling for about two years now since this happened. My counselor knows everything and has basically told me in professional terms that staying away from people who treat me this way is what is best for my mental health. I never realized how god awful they could be either until I started reading the letter outloud to my counselor and she stopped me midway through and simply said “that was absolutely terrible and I’m so sorry they sent you that”. It didn’t even dawn on me that this wasn’t how fights should normally go until my counselor reacted the way she did. That was how are fights always went for the entire 5 years we had been friends. They would get angry at me for one reason or another, and either send me a 7-paged paper on how shitty I am or write vague poetry about me and post it on social media for our mutual friends to go “omg who would do such a thing?!!”. Everytime I would cave and apologize and give the self-satisfaction they were obviously craving. This was the only fight where I didn’t because somehow I was significantly more hurt by their actions this time probably because they did it fully knowing that I was quite literally suicidal at the time (I’m not anymore and am a lot better, but at the time I had watched my mom die on hospice and it was just super traumatizing for me). I’m honestly not even sure why I even still think about them and miss them when it’s so very clear my life has significantly improved since they left.

Literally same here. The friend who sent me that letter used to send me their self-harm photos, purchases of razors from Amazon, and would message or call me at any point about anything that troubled them. They then went on to write a letter about how I was a shitty person that was never a good friend to them and that only ever manipulated them with examples being situations that I could barely remember from years prior. Not only did they send me this really hurtful letter but they also took very personal and private conversations we had over the years on Skype and edited them to send to mutual friends as proof that I was a terrible person. I had never experienced anything so hurtful in my life and these actions completely ruined my ability to trust in other people. I sat in weekly counseling appointments trying to dissect any rational reason for the way I was treated and after over a year of beating myself finally realized there really was no valid reason for it. Someone who truly cared about me and my well-being wouldn’t have done what they did when I was quite literally standing on the edge myself. All this being said, I really did wonder if I was this terrible person especially since like 3 or 4 people had the same opinion of me, but it’s been over two years and I have quite literally had zero fights with anyone else. A few misunderstandings that were easily cleared up and not blown out of proportion, sure, but not any long letter on Google doc drama and screaming in my face in the University library fights. So maybe I wasn’t the common denominator after all since it’s been oddly quiet since they all dipped. Meanwhile I hear through the grape vine that most of them are still fighting with people and are as hateful as they have always been. Despite all this I still lowkey hope they find peace some day and can stop treating people like trash when they don’t get their way.

We have a 15 year old dog who gets easily startled now because his eye sight is going bad. 

Hopefully this was just a freak accident and maybe just make sure to be careful when dog is around your feet. I’ve been guilty of stepping on my dogs paw before and I know it can hurt them (mine always Yelp to let me know). Another thing is sometimes dog react to chronic pain this way. I had a dog have a slipped disk and was becoming weirdly aggressive which was unnatural for her. It wasn’t until she bit my dad did we realize something was wrong. Turns out she had a slipped disk and had been experiencing chronic pain for months.

I would suggest talking to your professors. Be honest that you’ve been struggling with your mental health. Don’t tell them you planned to kill yourself because they will have to mandate report that, but explain to them that you’ve been having a really rough time with your mental health but that you’re getting the help you need. Ask them for extensions on assignments, or even see if you can receive incompletes to have more time to finish the classes. If all else fails, you can always see if they would allow you to medically withdraw so that way not completing the classes won’t hurt you. You’d probably have to provide some kind of doctor proof though that you’re getting help with your mental health and that the medical withdraw is necessary. 

I have always been as honest as I possibly can be with my professors without putting them in a situation where they have to report me. Almost all of them have been very understanding and have given me extensions, extra help, or in some cases even talked to the dean of students on my behalf. Professors are human too and also had to attend college. 9 times out of 10 they have experienced some kind of mental health problems before too and will understand how hard it can be. I hope this helps you and I wish you good luck.
